I found 6 likely bugs in this change. The two most serious can corrupt files on disk when Cline edits them. These findings come from reading the diff and the surrounding code. I didn't run anything, so the jschardet return values below are from its documented behaviour.

- **`src/integrations/editor/DiffViewProvider.ts:237` (high)** — jschardet labels plain-ASCII files `"ascii"`, so the file gets re-encoded as ASCII after the edit. Any non-ASCII character the edit adds (e.g. "café", emoji, CJK text) is written to disk as `?`, while the model is told the file contains the correct text.
- **`src/integrations/editor/DiffViewProvider.ts:237` (medium)** — The code checks for `"utf8"`, but jschardet returns `"UTF-8"`, which lowercases to `"utf-8"`, so the check never matches. Every UTF-8 file is therefore written a second time after VS Code saves it. That second write strips a leading BOM and replaces the trailing whitespace/newlines VS Code saved, so the disk no longer matches the open editor.
- **`src/integrations/editor/DiffViewProvider.ts:49` (medium)** — The detected encoding is used however low jschardet's confidence is. A short UTF-8 file can be guessed as windows-1252 or ISO-8859-x: it is shown to the model as garbled text, then rewritten in that legacy encoding, which corrupts a valid file.
- **`src/integrations/editor/DiffViewProvider.ts:238` (medium)** — Writing the file directly behind VS Code's back leaves the open editor showing different content from the disk. Also, rejecting an edit still saves through VS Code without re-encoding, so a Shift_JIS file is silently converted to UTF-8 on revert.
- **`src/integrations/misc/extract-text.ts:30` (medium)** — The binary-file check now only runs when jschardet returns no encoding, but it usually returns some guess for binary data. Small `.png`/`.zip` files are then decoded and fed to the model as garbage instead of being rejected.
- **`src/integrations/misc/extract-text.ts:26` (low)** — The whole file is now read into memory before the 300KB limit is checked. Previously the size was checked first and binary files were never read. A multi-GB log or binary can exhaust memory or throw before the size error appears.
